definition.text: A flammable carbon or hydrocarbon material formed naturally in the Earth's crust from the buried remains of prehistoric organisms.

facts.text: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are burnt for heating, to power engines and to generate electricity; some are refined into kerosene, gasoline and diesel or turned into plastics and other petrochemicals.
Because they take millions of years to form, fossil fuels are non-renewable resources.
In 2023, 77% of world primary energy consumption and over 60% of electricity supply came from fossil fuels.
Over 70% of human greenhouse gas emissions in 2022 was CO2 from burning fossil fuels.

Burning them has negative externalities: CO2 that speeds climate change, plus particulates, smog and acid rain; air pollution from fossil fuels in 2018 was estimated to cost US$2.9 trillion, 3.3% of global GDP.

definition.text: The geological process by which buried dead organisms become coal, oil and gas.

facts.text: Plankton that died and sedimented in anoxic conditions began forming petroleum and natural gas by anaerobic decomposition; terrestrial plants tend to form coal and methane.
Burial under sediment brought heat and pressure that turned organic matter into kerogen and then liquid and gaseous hydrocarbons.
The energy released in combustion is still photosynthetic in origin.

title: Health effects of fossil fuel pollution

definition.text: The illness and premature death caused by inhaling particulates and other air pollution from burning fossil fuels.

facts.text: Effects include premature death, acute respiratory illness, aggravated asthma, chronic bronchitis and decreased lung function; the poor, very young, very old and those with respiratory disease are most at risk.
Global deaths from fossil-fuel air pollution were estimated at over 8 million in 2018 (nearly 1 in 5 deaths), 10.2 million in 2019 and 5.13 million excess deaths in 2023.
Fossil fuels cause the highest greenhouse gas emissions and are the most dangerous to health; modern renewables appear safer and cleaner.

definition.text: The impact of fossil fuel prices on inflation.

facts.text: Economists have pointed to energy prices as the main reason for high inflation in 2022; transport, food and shipping prices rise sharply when fossil fuel prices do.
Mark Zandi says fossil fuel prices have driven every big inflation episode since WWII.
Gernot Wagner argues commodities are volatile energy sources, whereas renewable technologies get relatively cheaper over time.
